expectations.text: States that a written agreement or reminder is not enforcement
expectations.evidence: every mechanism you used so far is rung 0 — a comment, a wiki page, a Slack pin, and a standup mention are all 'training,' and training degrades. Nothing enforces the rule

expectations.text: Recommends a pre-commit hook to run the formatter automatically
expectations.evidence: Formatter as a pre-commit hook, not documentation — `prettier --check` / `black --check` (or `--write` if you want it auto-fixing)

expectations.text: Notes that pre-commit is bypassable with --no-verify and must be backed by a CI check
expectations.evidence: it's bypassable with `--no-verify`, so it's not the real enforcement, just the fast feedback loop... The same check as a required CI check — this is the one that actually matters, because CI can't be --no-verify'd

expectations.text: Recommends a type check as a required CI check
expectations.evidence: run `prettier --check` / `tsc --noEmit` / `mypy --strict` in CI and mark it required in branch protection

expectations.text: Recommends baselining or ratcheting rather than enforcing across the whole repo at once
expectations.evidence: Either scope the check to changed files (`git diff --name-only origin/main... | xargs mypy`) or generate a baseline of current violations and fail CI only on *new* ones

expectations.text: Notes that branch protection is what makes a CI check actually required
expectations.evidence: Without branch protection, a required check is just a suggestion

expectations.text: Recommends the failure message tell the developer how to fix it
expectations.evidence: this function is missing a return type annotation — add `-> None` (or the right type) and push again gets fixed; a bare `error: rule violated` gets bypassed or ignored

expectations.text: Does not primarily recommend rewriting CONTRIBUTING.md, more reminders, or more discipline
expectations.evidence: The fix isn't a better reminder, it's a gate
